title: Vocabulary: understanding others
keyIdea: Some words help us understand other people. Similar means alike in some way; different means not the same, and two people can be both. Empathy is feeling with someone: imagining their feeling and staying with them. Sympathy is feeling sorry for them. Perspective is how things look from where someone is. Fair means everyone gets an equal chance. Kind and care mean being gentle and helping. A community is a group of people who share a place, and inclusion makes sure everyone belongs.

kid: Mia and Raj are both 7. They both have a dog. That makes them similar. Mia loves pizza and Raj plays cricket. That makes them different. Two people can be similar and different at the same time.
Leo drops his ice cream and cries. Empathy is when you think, 'I would be sad too,' and you stay with him. Sympathy is when you just feel sorry for him. Empathy feels with. Sympathy feels for.
Perspective is how things look from where you are. If you sit on one side of a toy, you see one side. Your friend on the other side sees something else. Feelings work like that too.
Fair means everyone gets a go. Kind means gentle words and help. Care means looking after someone. A community is a group who share a place, like your class. Everyone should feel they belong.
adult: This vocabulary sits in PSHE Relationships education at Key Stage 1 and in the IB PYP PSPE interactions strand. Children learn to use eight words: empathy, perspective, kind, fair, community, similar, different and care. They also start to tell empathy from sympathy, and use belonging and inclusion about their class.

A common mistake is to treat empathy and sympathy as the same. Sympathy is feeling sorry for someone, often from a distance. Empathy is imagining their feeling and staying with them. Another slip is thinking 'different' means 'not alike at all'. Two people can share some things and not others.

Young children often think others see what they see. Piaget's three-mountains task showed that taking another person's view grows with age. So start with something concrete, like a block with a different picture on each side, before talking about feelings. At this age, 'fair' means equal turns and equal chances.

In the lab your child sorts facts about Mia and Raj into a Venn diagram, sorts replies to Leo into empathy and sympathy, sits in three seats round a picture block, gives fair turns on a swing, and drags kind actions so a new girl, Sofi, joins the class community.

familyTip: When a character in a book is upset, ask: 'How would you feel? What could you say to show empathy?' Then find one way you are similar to a friend and one way you are different.

visual.caption: Empathy or sympathy? Drag each reply, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: I'd be scared too. I'll come with you.
You look sad. Do you want a hug?
That must hurt. I'll sit with you.
I know how that feels. Shall we fix it?

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort Mia and Raj in a Venn diagram, tell empathy from sympathy, sit in three seats, give fair turns, and help Sofi belong.

practice.prompt: Zac falls over. Amy says, 'Ouch, I'd cry too. Let me help you up.' What is Amy showing?
practice.hint: Does Amy imagine Zac's feeling and stay with him?
practice.explain: Empathy. Amy imagines how Zac feels ('I'd cry too') and stays to help. Just saying 'poor you' would be sympathy.

practice.prompt: Ben and Lucy both have {n} letters in their name. Is that a way they are similar or different?
practice.explain: Similar. Both names have {n} letters, so they share it. Similar means alike in some way.

practice.prompt: {n} children want the red bike. What is the fair way?
choices: The biggest child has it all day
practice.hint: Fair means everyone gets an equal chance.
practice.explain: Taking turns is fair, because all {n} children get a go. Keeping it all day gives one child more than the others.

practice.prompt: You see a cat on your side of a box. Your friend sits on the other side. What can you say?
choices: She must see a cat too
practice.hint: What you see depends on where you sit.
practice.explain: She might see something different. That is her perspective: how things look from where she is.

choices: Feeling with someone: imagining how they feel
pool.hint: Empathy feels with. Sympathy feels for.
pool.explain: Empathy is imagining how someone feels and staying with them. Feeling sorry for them is sympathy.

pool.prompt: Nia says, 'Oh dear, poor you,' and walks on. What is that?
pool.hint: Did Nia stay and imagine the feeling?
pool.explain: Sympathy: Nia feels sorry, but does not stay or imagine the feeling. Empathy would sound like 'I'd be upset too.'

pool.prompt: Tom has {n} brothers and Ali has none. Is that a way they are similar or different?
pool.explain: Different. Tom has {n} brothers and Ali has none, so it is not the same. They can still be similar in other ways.

choices: A group of people who share a place and help each other
pool.hint: Think of your class or your street.
pool.explain: A community is a group of people who share a place, like a class, a street or a club.

pool.prompt: A new girl stands alone at playtime. What would help her belong?
choices: Ask her name and invite her to play
pool.explain: Asking her name and inviting her to play helps her belong. Waiting leaves her outside the group.

pool.prompt: There are {n} stickers for {n} children. What is fair?
choices: All of them for one child
pool.hint: Fair means an equal chance for everyone.
pool.explain: One each is fair: {n} stickers shared by {n} children gives everyone the same.

pool.prompt: Kai helps his grandad carry the shopping. Which word fits?
pool.hint: Which word means looking after someone?
pool.explain: Care. Kai is looking after his grandad by helping him.
